content:
Redwood Inference — SOC 2 Overview (Draft)
Version: v0.8 (Draft)
Last updated: 2026-02-14
Owner: GRC (Olga Petrov)

Purpose
This one‑pager is intended to help customers and prospects understand Redwood Inference’s SOC 2 posture and how our controls relate to the way we build and operate our inference platform.

Important notes (read first)
- Redwood is not “SOC 2 certified.” SOC 2 is an attestation report issued by an independent auditor.
- The SOC 2 report is confidential and is shared under NDA with qualified customers/prospects.
- Deployment modes differ. Some controls are implemented by Redwood, and some are shared with the customer depending on Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

At a glance
- Attestation: SOC 2 Type II (report available under NDA)
- Trust Services Criteria addressed (see report for exact scope):
  - Security (Common Criteria)
  - Availability (if included in your shared report)
  - Confidentiality (if included in your shared report)
- Report period: Most recent annual Type II period ending 2025-12-31 (exact dates and coverage are in the report)

What’s in scope (high-level)
The SOC 2 report covers Redwood’s security program and the relevant people, processes, and systems used to operate our customer-facing services.

In practical terms, this typically includes:
- Corporate security program governance (policies, risk management, training)
- Identity and access management for production systems
- Secure SDLC and change management for the Redwood platform
- Production operations, monitoring, and incident response processes
- Vendor/subprocessor management process

Service boundary / product mapping (non-authoritative summary)
The SOC 2 scope is aligned to Redwood-operated systems that support our platform. Exact system descriptions, boundaries, and exclusions are defined in the report.

- Hosted API (Redwood API + Redwood Console)
  - Redwood operates the service in our cloud environments and is responsible for the security controls in-scope for the service.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity)
  - Redwood operates dedicated capacity for a customer within Redwood-managed infrastructure (with customer-specific isolation controls).
  - Control ownership remains primarily with Redwood for the managed service components.

- Private (VPC / on‑prem)
  - Private deployments involve shared responsibility.
  - Redwood’s SOC 2 report covers Redwood’s organizational controls and our controlled SDLC / support processes.
  - Customer-controlled infrastructure and customer operational procedures (e.g., their network perimeter, host hardening, SIEM operations) may be outside Redwood’s report scope.
  - For customer-specific confirmations, route questions through the evidence request process.

Control themes (how SOC 2 control areas show up in the product)
Below are common SOC 2 themes and where customers typically see them reflected in Redwood’s platform capabilities.

1) Security governance and risk management
- Security policies and standards, security awareness training, risk assessments
- Vendor/subprocessor management and periodic reviews

2) Access controls (logical access)
- Centralized identity and role management for Redwood employees and contractors
- Production access governed by least privilege and logged/monitored
- Customer-facing controls (capability varies by deployment and plan):
  - SSO/SAML support for Console access
  - SCIM provisioning (where applicable)
  - Role-based access control (RBAC) for Console and API operations

3) Encryption and key management
- In transit: TLS for service endpoints
- At rest: encryption for data stored in Redwood-managed systems
- Key management: managed key infrastructure with KMS integrations; customer-specific key options may be available depending on deployment mode (Dedicated/Private) and commercial packaging

4) Logging, monitoring, and auditability
- Platform monitoring, alerting, and operational logging
- Customer-visible audit logging (capability varies by deployment and configuration):
  - Administrative events (e.g., auth events, key configuration, access changes)
  - Export options (e.g., to customer SIEM/S3) may be available depending on deployment mode

5) Vulnerability management and secure development
- Secure SDLC practices (reviews, approvals, change control)
- Vulnerability scanning and remediation processes
- Penetration testing and third-party assessments (details available under NDA as applicable)

6) Incident response and business continuity
- Incident response procedures, escalation, and communications process
- Business continuity / disaster recovery planning for Redwood-operated services (see report for specifics)

Customer data, prompts, and model training (frequently asked)
- Data processing: Redwood processes customer prompts/inputs and outputs to provide the service.
- Model training: Redwood does not use customer content to train public or generally-available models by default. Any exception would require explicit customer agreement and documented terms.
- Retention: Data retention and log retention vary by deployment mode and configuration; see the separate Data Retention & Deletion Overview for customer-facing details.

How to request the SOC 2 report (under NDA)
1) Confirm an NDA is in place between your organization and Redwood (or request Redwood’s standard NDA).
2) Submit an evidence request through your Redwood account team or via the security evidence request intake:
   - Email: security@redwoodinference.com (or your AE/SE)
   - Include: company name, opportunity/customer name, requested artifact (“SOC 2 Type II report”), and due date.
3) Redwood GRC will respond with the report via approved secure sharing methods.

Typical turnaround time
- Standard requests: 3–5 business days after NDA confirmation
- Expedited requests: handled case-by-case based on deal timeline and GRC queue

What we can provide (typical SOC 2 evidence set)
- SOC 2 Type II report (under NDA)
- Customer-facing security overview and FAQ
- Subprocessor overview and security addendum/DPA materials (as applicable)
- Supporting policy summaries or additional evidence as approved (restricted items may require additional review)

What we do not provide
- Raw internal logs, source code, or highly sensitive internal security tooling details
- Customer-specific attestations outside the report scope without formal review/approval

Suggested RFP language (customer-safe)
“Redwood Inference maintains a SOC 2 Type II attestation report covering security controls relevant to the operation of its cloud services. The report is available to qualified customers and prospects under NDA upon request.”

Internal notes (remove before customer distribution)
- Validate the exact Trust Services Criteria included in the current report before sending externally (Security-only vs Security+Availability+Confidentiality).
- Ensure the stated report period matches the latest issued report.
- Ensure links in outbound emails point to the current Evidence Request Playbook and the latest Security FAQ.
